reason: The document history row 'Changes to body inspection size limits' says AWS WAF now supports larger body inspection size limits for some regional resources, dated March 7, 2024.

The FAQ says WAF charges are in addition to CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway and/or AppSync pricing; the CloudFront page says flat-rate plans combine CloudFront with multiple services into a monthly price (list includes AWS WAF and DDoS protection) and names pay-as-you-go as the alternative.

Under 'AWS managed rule group DDoS protection' the page says the advanced tier is offered through AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet and that its protection extends to CloudFront distributions, Application Load Balancers, and other AWS services supported by AWS WAF.
The FAQ answer to 'Is there a AWS WAF request limit?' states the claim word for word, and the next sentence says the requests are consolidated at the customer level, matching the per-customer scope.
The FAQ answer to 'How does AWS WAF block or allow traffic?' states the forward-for-inspection and block-or-allow-by-action behavior exactly as claimed.

The page says an IP set is a collection of IP addresses and ranges used together in a rule statement, that you first create the IPSet resource, then reference the set in an IP set rule statement in a web ACL or rule group.

The managed rule groups page says Bot Control, ATP and ACFP groups cost additional fees beyond basic WAF charges; on the DDoS page the Note 'You are charged additional fees when you use this managed rule group' follows the AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet paragraph it refers to.
The Note on the forwarded IP addresses page states the No match evaluation, the NOT conversion to Match, and that missing headers don't trigger fallback behavior, only invalid header values do.

The pricing page states the three charge dimensions, no upfront commitments, and the in-addition-to list (CloudFront, Cognito, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Shield Advanced); the CloudFront page supports the flat-rate monthly price and pay-as-you-go as the alternative.

The quotas table (per organization in a single Region) gives 12 requests per second for us-east-1, us-west-2 and eu-west-1 and 6 for other Regions, and the paragraph above it says these fixed organization quotas can't be changed.
